Chateaubriand, because it's the steak you're actually looking for when you order a filet. You just don't know that, because it's not offered at your typical steakhouse.

As for how to cook it? A good steak should be seared on the outside but otherwise bleu throughout. No sauce, because sauce is for bad steak. Just some salt, pepper, and a little garlic. Maybe a few shallots, if you like onions.

This steak will run you nearly $100 in a restaurant, and most of that is for the meat. You'll pay $30-40 per pound at a butcher, and a proper chateaubriand cut is 20oz. So save it for that big promotion, or an anniversary that's divisible by 10, but order one at least ONCE in your life, because life is too short to spend thinking that filet or ribeye is the pinnacle of steak.

Tested In-Depth: Oculus Rift vs. HTC Vive

I wonder if rift will have better quality control for games than vive. steam catalog of independent studios is crap. Sure there are a few bright spots but overall we see a lot of abandoned betas from scammers. Rift might not have that prpblem
I doubt either company will have any control over the games that take advantage of VR. Neither company requires a review process for games that use their respective SDKs.

The TL;DR is that the Rift wins in just about every category when dealing with image quality, comfort, and tracking. I see this as a product of the Rift being in the R&D phase for longer. I imagine the Vive will eventually catch up on some of these things - tracking in particular on the Vive is a problem as it sometimes loses tracking. This is probably something that can be solved with software.

So far the only killer feature of the Vive is roomscale, which is definitely compelling but also impractical (you need a reasonable amount of space near your computer to get the most out of this) for most people. Additionally you're dragging a cable around which I could see causing some issues. Roomscale will make a lot more sense once the headset is able to be wireless - unfortunately I don't see this happening for a while.

Overall, this is a very good video if you want an objective technical comparison of the two headsets instead of an opinionated political shitfest.

The video is great, but the main thing I took from this is that both are pretty good but neither will totally blow anyone away until they make enough improvements to make them worth it for the average consumer

Objectively speaking, the rift is better than the Vive in all features that are supported by both. I do agree that some of it is splitting hairs so fine that it may as well be a draw, but some of it is not. Comfort is really important if you're going to be using a headset for hours at a time, and I think the Rift does a better overall job delivering on this.
